paitṛka-mantras
(‘sacred formulae associated with the पितृस् or manes’)
------------------------------------------
During the times of the Ṛgveda persons who died here were believed to go to the पितृलोक (world of manes) and live there in subtle bodies. They were propitiated through certain rites (now well-known as śrāddha) wherein oblations were offered for them into a duly consecrated fire.
The fourteen mantras of the Ṛgveda (10.1

) used in such rites are called ‘paitṛka-mantras’.
The ṛṣi or sage of this group of mantras is शङ्ख-Yāmāyana. The पितृस् (manes) are the देवतास् or deities. Triṣṭup and जगती are the metres used.
These mantras are recited during the ड़ुनेरल् रितेस् performed in the śmaśāna (cremation ground).
The first seven mantras are prayers to the पितृस् for accepting the offerings and protecting the performer. The eighth one is addressed to यम, the god of death, to accept the offerings given to him. The next two (and 12th to 14th) are an invitation to अग्नि, the god of fire and a prayer to him.
It is interesting to note that in these mantras the पितृस् are categorised into three groups: uttama (the best), madhyama (middling) and adhama (the lowest).
